# Incise 0.2.0

Incise 0.2.0 turns measured model behavior into safer, model-aware Markdown editing without weakening the byte-preserving core.

## Gemma: 99.2% correct with automatic routing

The new Pi `auto` profile identifies the active model once and enables only capabilities backed by a passing model-family evaluation. In the preregistered Gemma full-profile run:

- 475 of 479 completed paired cases were correct (99.2%).
- All 200 routed cases were correct.
- All 60 table, 100 list, 110 frontmatter, and 60 table-read cases were correct.
- 145 of 149 completed section cases were correct; the other four were loud refusals.
- No silent corruption or data loss was observed.

One of the 480 attempted cases, `rename-setext`, persistently timed out and is excluded from the 479-case paired denominator. These figures describe the recorded Gemma/Pi benchmark conditions, not every model or prompt.

Enable the measured Gemma behavior with:

```bash
INCISE_PROFILE=auto pi
```

## MiniCPM: focused compatibility and safer experimentation

`table-add-row` now accepts MiniCPM's unambiguous singleton-object `values` shape while preserving normal column and type validation. The targeted table arm improved from 9/18 to 18/18, including 9/9 calls that used the compatibility path, with no silent corruption or data loss.

The optional `minicpm-list` Pi profile adds inspect-then-edit list handling. Its real Pi run completed 16/21 requests; every executed edit was correct, while five requests made no tool call. It remains experimental and opt-in:

```bash
INCISE_PROFILE=minicpm-list pi
```

For general MiniCPM work, the standard profile remains the recommendation.

## Narrower tools and stronger safeguards

- Added structured list and frontmatter reads with exact, copyable item text, nesting, flattened key paths, types, values, and document hashes.
- Added an opt-in `safe-small` schema with action-specific table, list, section, and frontmatter tools.
- Added structured repair data alongside human-readable refusals.
- Added subtree confirmation for destructive section deletion and existence guards for frontmatter writes.
- Kept risky generic section operations out of the small-model profile.

The Rust core still has no dependencies and remains checked byte-for-byte against the independent Python oracle. This release passed 111,662 differential cases, the invariant suite, and replay checks over 22,617 recorded tool calls.

## Pi and Hermes integration

Pi gains the model-aware `auto` profile plus conservative host-owned routes for the request shapes that passed preregistered evaluation. Unrecognized requests fall back to the standard measured tools.

Hermes continues to expose the standard eight-tool interface by default and can opt into the twelve-tool safe-small composition. Plugin Doctor now reports the selected binary, and development checkouts prefer their current build over a stale binary on `PATH`.

## Install and upgrade

Pi includes a matching native binary on supported macOS and Linux platforms:

```bash
pi install npm:pi-incise
```

Install the CLI directly from crates.io:

```bash
cargo install incise-cli --version 0.2.0 --locked
```

The tag-driven release also publishes four platform archives and a version-matched Hermes plugin archive. All Rust crates, npm packages, native packages, and integration metadata are pinned to 0.2.0.
